click: A dry button press: a word lands, a card is chosen, a UI step is confirmed. The default small accent.
tick: A very small, very short beat: counters, list items appearing one after another, a timer step.
pop: A rounded bubble: an element or emoji pops into the frame. Tags low, mid, high give the pitch.
toggle: A switch flipping on or off (tags on, off): settings, before/after, yes/no moments.
type: One key of typing: text being typed or a terminal line. Play several variants in a row for a burst.
swish: A short airy flick (under 0.3 s): a card slides, a small element wipes across.
whoosh: A fast pass-by (0.3 to 1.2 s): a scene cut, a big element flying in. Tags short and long.
riser: A rise in pitch or noise that builds tension towards a hit (1 to 4 s). Tags 1s to 4s give its length.
swell: A reversed-cymbal style build that peaks at its last moment: lead-in to a reveal or title.
drop: A falling sweep or sub drop: the number crashes, the price falls, the mood turns down.
impact: A hard hit with body, with a mid-range thump so it still works on a phone speaker: reveals, big numbers.
thump: A low, short body hit with no ring: a soft landing under a pop, a punch on a cut.
shimmer: A bright airy wash, glassy and sustained: something precious, magical or clean appears.
sparkle: A quick run of high bell-like sparks: a highlight, a glint on a logo, a small win.
success: A positive resolve (0.4 to 1.5 s): a problem is solved, a check goes green. Tag resolve is the closing chord.
error: A negative buzz or low double-note: something fails, is blocked or is wrong.
notify: A phone-style alert or message ping: a notification arrives, an alert in a story.
ding: A single clean bell or coin note: a point is made, a price is revealed, a value is added.
glitch: Digital stutter and static: a hack, a corrupted frame, a cut to something broken.
rustle: Cloth, paper or air texture with no pitch: a soft movement under a slide, a page turn.
scratch: A quick vinyl or scrape movement: a record-stop moment, a rewind, a sudden stop of the narrative.
bed: A quiet loopable background (looped by the assembler): tension, tech hum or air under narration.
